title: Pit Crew: Shift Catchup - 03/01 (sprint ops scratch)
content:
Quick shift catchup — PIT CREW notes (working draft)

Shift window: 2026-03-01 07:00 -> 15:00 PT
Primary oncall: Maya Chen (me)
Followup / backup: Ethan Patel (12:00->end)
Purpose: lightweight runbook fragments, temporary mitigations, and things I keep restarting from memory. Not polished; copy useful bits into formal runbook later.

Summary / state at handoff:
- No active Sev1s. Two flaky alerts still firing intermittently: latency-surge-alert (happens ~1x/day) and kv-cache-miss-spike (sporadic, small).
- Canary models running fine; small tail latency increase on model-x-7b-v1 after 09:30 (probable worker restart noise).
- Dedicated pool (dp-west-1) at 68% of provisioned GPU capacity; autoscaler bumped 2 nodes at 02:10 earlier this week — confirmed healthy.

Recent incidents & notes (short):
- 2026-02-28 23:40: transient 503s for /v1/generate in hosted-api-eu; root cause: nginx worker OOM on host infra-03. Kernel OOM killed a coupla workers. (See OPS-914)
  - mitigation applied: raised nginx worker_rlimit_nofile to 65536 on infra-03 and rolled out to infra-04. No repeat since.
- 2026-03-01 09:10: model-x-7b-v1 increase p95 from 220ms -> 410ms for ~12 minutes. Investigation hint: many small requests with short sequences = batching/kv-cache path thrash. I forced a small cache-warm on 09:20 and p95 dropped.

Temp runbook steps (most frequently used during this shift):
- Quick triage for 503s (hosted api):
  1) Check PagerDuty/Slack alert for service and correlation id.
  2) ssh to host reported by alert (if infra-host): ssh ubuntu@infra-03
  3) top / dmesg | tail -> look for OOM killer or segfaults
  4) systemctl status redwood-nginx.service && journalctl -u redwood-nginx -n 200
  5) If worker processes killed, restart nginx gracefully: sudo systemctl restart redwood-nginx && monitor 2m
  6) If problem persists, rollback last nginx config change (check /etc/nginx/conf.d/ and /var/log/nginx/reload-history) and notify infra team.

- Quick triage for high model tail latency (serving-runtime):
  1) Check serving dashboard: per-model p50/p95/p99, and per-host CPU/GPU utilization
  2) kubectl -n serving get pods -l model=model-x-7b-v1 -o wide -> find pods on nodes with high load
  3) kubectl logs <pod> -c runtime -n serving --tail=200 | grep -i 'batch' or 'kvcache'
  4) If mem pressure on pod: kubectl describe pod <pod> -> OOM events? If yes, scale down replicas and roll nodes via replacement (coord with infra).
  5) Temporary mitigation: disable small-request aggressive batching for model-x config (toggle in configmap: serving/batching-config) or apply small KV warm on sample prefixes.

Useful commands (copy/paste friendly):
- get heavy pods: kubectl -n serving get pods --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount | tail -n 30
- fetch recent errors for model-x: kubectl logs -n serving -l model=model-x-7b-v1 -c runtime --since=30m | grep -E "(ERROR|WARN|kvcache|batch)"
- bump nginx fd limit (temporary restart): sudo sed -i 's/worker_rlimit_nofile .*/worker_rlimit_nofile 65536;/' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf && sudo systemctl restart redwood-nginx

Open follow-ups (things to not forget):
- Investigate why kv-cache-miss-spike correlates with small-sequence requests from route /v1/embeddings; could be a prefix-hammer from a single client. Add per-token debug logging for one minute during low traffic window. (ticket: ONCALL-78)
- Add more robust alert for 'nginx worker OOM' rather than generic 503 threshold. Suggest: dmesg OOM string -> alert in Prometheus via node-exporter logs.
- Roll a configuration change to serving batching defaults for model-x in staging first (test with synthetic short-seq load), then to canary, then prod. // Create PR and reference infra PR above.

Notes to self / heuristics I use often:
- If p95 spikes and GPUs are <70% util, look at batching configuration and KV cache heatmap before blaming hardware.
- Many user-generated micro-requests will kill batching efficiency — the runtime will spin lots of tiny batches and p95 jumps. Consider small request coalescing as mitigation.
- If you see "rpc hang for 30s" in logs and only one host, check network interface counters (ethtool -S) and kernel ring buffers.

Escalation list (quick dial):
- Infra lead: Ethan Patel (pagerduty +1) -> +1-555-0134
- Serving runtime owner: Lena Rodriguez -> slack @lena or mobile +1-555-0177
- Security oncall (for weird auth anomalies): Priya Gupta -> slack #sec-oncall

Temporary patches we applied this week (record):
- increased nginx worker_rlimit_nofile on infra-03/04
- disabled aggressive batching for model-y-2b on canary to prevent backlog (will re-evaluate)
- added per-route slowlog for /v1/embeddings at 2s threshold (staging).

Decisions to formalize later:
- Add a runbook section for "kv-cache-miss-spike" with step-by-step collection commands and a small playbook to warm caches rather than restart pods.
- Create targeted alerting for "increased per-host small-batch rate" and tie it to a runbook that triggers auto-aggregation of tiny requests for 5m.

Random scratchpad / ideas:
- Build a small synthetic load test that simulates 100k short-seq embedding requests over 10m to reproduce cache churn. Use that to tune batching.
- Small script: ./scripts/cache_warm_cli.sh --model model-x-7b-v1 --prefixes sample_prefixes.txt (uses admin token) — keep script in infra/tools

Things I want the next oncall to check within first 30 minutes:
- Verify no repeating 503s in the last hour via logs/observability
- Confirm dp-west-1 pool utilization hasn't spiked >90% overnight
- Look at latest canary-run outputs for model-x after config tweak at 09:25

Unresolved questions / TODOs (short):
- Who triggered the high small-request pattern Wed 02/26 around 11:02? Trace logs show source X-Client-ID: 0x3a7 but no linked token yet.
- Confirm whether autoscaler bump was due to real load or a misconfigured probe (investigate k8s probe flapping).

If you pick this up, feel free to ping me directly on Slack (mchen) — I'll be online for another hour to help triage handoff issues.

-- end of scratchpad --

(If this doc helps, move good bits into eng-sre/runbooks/serving-runtime-kvcache.md and mark as reviewed.)
